paraphrase: Arjuna says he sees ill omens and no good in killing his kinsmen; he wants neither victory, kingdom nor pleasures, and would not kill them even for rule over the three worlds, let alone for the earth.
speaker: Arjuna

paraphrase: Arjuna argues that killing these aggressors would bring sin; with the destruction of a family its ancient family dharmas perish, adharma overcomes the family, its women are corrupted, mixture of varṇas arises, the ancestors fall for want of offerings of rice-balls and water, and those who destroy family dharma dwell in hell, as he has heard.
speaker: Arjuna

paraphrase: Arjuna says his nature is struck by the fault of pity (kārpaṇya) and his mind is confused about dharma; he asks Kṛṣṇa to tell him decisively what is better, declaring: 'I am your disciple; teach me, who have taken refuge in you.'
speaker: Arjuna

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa says Arjuna grieves for those who should not be grieved for, yet speaks words of wisdom; the wise grieve neither for those whose breath has gone nor for those whose breath has not gone.

paraphrase: As the embodied one passes in this body through childhood, youth and old age, so it passes to another body; the steady person is not deluded by this.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The contacts of the senses with their objects, giving cold and heat, pleasure and pain, come and go and are impermanent; endure them. The person whom these do not disturb, the same in pleasure and pain, the steady one, is fit for immortality.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The unreal has no being and the real never ceases to be; the boundary between the two has been seen by the seers of truth.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it, water does not wet it, wind does not dry it; it is uncuttable, unburnable, not to be wetted or dried; eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable and primeval.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: It is called unmanifest, unthinkable and unchangeable; knowing it to be such, you should not grieve.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Even if you think it is constantly born and constantly dies, you should not grieve: for death is certain for the born and birth certain for the dead; beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in the middle and unmanifest again at their end — what is there to lament?
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Some see it as a wonder, some speak of it as a wonder, some hear of it as a wonder; and even having heard of it, no one knows it.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: Parallel theme: Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.2.7.

paraphrase: Considering your own dharma you should not waver, for nothing is better for a kṣatriya than a righteous war; happy are the kṣatriyas who meet such a war, come unsought as an open door to heaven; if you do not fight this righteous battle you will give up your own dharma and honour and incur sin.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: People will speak of your lasting dishonour, and for one who has been honoured dishonour is worse than death; slain, you will attain heaven; victorious, you will enjoy the earth; therefore arise, resolved to fight.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Treating alike pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, gird yourself for battle; thus you will not incur sin.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: This understanding has been declared to you in terms of Sāṃkhya; now hear it in terms of Yoga, joined with which you will cast off the bondage of action.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: In this no effort is lost and no reverse is incurred; even a little of this dharma protects from great fear.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Here the resolute understanding (vyavasāyātmikā buddhi) is one; the understandings of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The undiscerning, delighting in the words of the Veda and saying there is nothing else, full of desires and intent on heaven, speak flowery words that offer rebirth as the fruit of action and prescribe many special rites for enjoyment and power; in those attached to enjoyment and power, whose minds are carried away by these words, the resolute understanding is not established in samādhi.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The Vedas have the three guṇas as their domain; be free of the three guṇas, Arjuna — free from the pairs of opposites, ever abiding in sattva, free from acquiring and keeping, possessed of the self.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: As much use as there is in a reservoir when there is a flood of water on every side, so much is there in all the Vedas for a brāhmaṇa who knows.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: Commentators differ: Śaṅkara takes it as saying the limited fruits of ritual are included in the fruit of knowledge; others as ranking ritual below knowledge.

paraphrase: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits; let not the fruit of action be your motive, nor let your attachment be to inaction.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: One yoked with understanding casts off here both good and evil deeds; therefore yoke yourself to yoga: yoga is skill in action.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The wise, yoked with understanding, abandoning the fruit born of action and freed from the bondage of birth, go to the state free from sorrow.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: When your understanding crosses the thicket of delusion you will become indifferent to what has been heard and what is yet to be heard; when your understanding, bewildered by hearing (scripture), stands unmoving and steady in samādhi, then you will attain yoga.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The person of steady wisdom (sthitaprajña): asked how such a one speaks, sits and walks, Kṛṣṇa describes one who has given up all desires and is content in the self by the self; unperturbed in sorrow, without longing in pleasure, free of passion, fear and anger; unattached everywhere; withdrawing the senses from their objects as a tortoise its limbs; for whom even the taste for objects ceases on seeing the supreme; who, restraining the senses, sits intent on the Lord; who moves among objects without attraction and aversion and attains serenity; who is awake in what is night for all beings; who, like the ocean filled by rivers, is unmoved by desires entering him; who lives without longing, without 'mine' and without ego — this is the brāhmī sthiti, and one established in it even at death attains brahmanirvāṇa.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Arjuna asks: what is the description of one of steady wisdom, established in samādhi? How does one of steady mind speak, how sit, how walk?

paraphrase: When one gives up all the desires that have entered the mind and is content in the self by the self alone, then one is called a person of steady wisdom.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: One whose mind is not agitated in sorrows and who is free of longing in pleasures, from whom passion, fear and anger have gone, is called a sage of steady mind; one who is unattached everywhere, neither rejoicing nor hating on meeting with good or ill, has established wisdom.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs on every side, one withdraws the senses from their objects, one's wisdom is established.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Sense-objects turn away from the embodied one who abstains from them, but the taste for them remains; even the taste turns away when the supreme is seen.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The turbulent senses carry off by force the mind even of a wise man who strives; restraining them all, one should sit yoked, intent on me; one whose senses are under control has established wisdom.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: For a person dwelling on sense-objects attachment to them arises; from attachment desire is born, from desire anger; from anger comes delusion, from delusion the loss of memory, from loss of memory the destruction of understanding, and from the destruction of understanding one perishes.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

The mind that follows the roving senses carries away one's wisdom as the wind a ship on the waters; therefore one whose senses are withdrawn from their objects has established wisdom.

paraphrase: What is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake; that in which beings are awake is night for the sage who sees.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The person who abandons all desires and moves about free from longing, without the sense of 'mine' and without ego, attains peace.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: This is the brāhmī state; attaining it one is not deluded; abiding in it even at the time of death, one reaches brahmanirvāṇa.

paraphrase: Arjuna asks: if you hold understanding to be superior to action, why do you urge me to this terrible deed? With seemingly mixed words you confuse my understanding; tell me the one thing by which I may reach the good.
speaker: Arjuna

paraphrase: Of old I declared a twofold path in this world: the yoga of knowledge for the Sāṃkhyas and the yoga of action for the yogins.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: The Gītā's own statement of plural paths — an anchor for the principle of path by temperament (P3).

paraphrase: Not by abstaining from actions does a person attain freedom from action (naiṣkarmya), nor by mere renunciation does one reach perfection.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: No one can remain even for a moment without acting; everyone is made to act helplessly by the guṇas born of prakṛti.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: One who restrains the organs of action but sits dwelling in mind on sense-objects is deluded and called a hypocrite; but one who controls the senses by the mind and, unattached, undertakes the yoga of action with the organs of action, excels.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Do your prescribed action, for action is better than inaction; even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: This world is bound by action other than action done for the sake of sacrifice; for that purpose perform action, free from attachment.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: In the beginning Prajāpati created beings together with sacrifice and said: by this you shall multiply; nourish the gods with it and they will nourish you; one who enjoys their gifts without offering to them is a thief; the good who eat the remains of sacrifice are freed from all faults, while those who cook only for themselves eat sin; beings come from food, food from rain, rain from sacrifice, sacrifice from action, action from Brahman (the Veda), and Brahman from the Imperishable — so the all-pervading Brahman is established in sacrifice; one who does not turn the wheel thus set in motion lives in vain.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: But for the person who delights in the self, is satisfied in the self and content in the self alone, there is nothing that has to be done; he has no purpose in what is done or not done here, nor any dependence on any being.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Therefore, unattached, always perform the action that must be done; for by performing action without attachment a person attains the supreme.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: By action alone Janaka and others attained perfection; you should act also with a view to the holding together of the world (lokasaṃgraha); whatever the best person does, others do, and the world follows the standard he sets.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: There is nothing in the three worlds that I must do, nothing unattained to be attained, yet I engage in action; if I did not act unwearied, people would follow my path; these worlds would perish if I did not act, and I would be the author of confusion and destroy these beings.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: As the unwise act attached to action, so the wise should act unattached, wishing to hold the world together; the wise should not unsettle the understanding of the ignorant who are attached to action, but, acting yoked, should engage them in all actions.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: An explicit instruction to teach according to the hearer's condition — an anchor for the principle of the student's stage (P4).

paraphrase: Actions are performed in every way by the guṇas of prakṛti; one deluded by ego thinks 'I am the doer'. But one who knows the truth about the divisions of guṇas and actions, knowing that guṇas act upon guṇas, is not attached.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Renouncing all actions in me, with your mind on the self, free from desire and from the sense of 'mine', your fever gone — fight.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Those who constantly follow this teaching of mine with faith and without cavil are freed from actions; but those who cavil and do not follow it, know them to be lost.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Even a person of knowledge acts according to his own nature; beings follow nature — what will restraint accomplish?
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: Commentators reconcile this with 3.34 and 6.35: nature is not to be forcibly suppressed but one should not come under the sway of attraction and aversion.

paraphrase: Attraction and aversion are seated in each sense toward its object; one should not come under their sway, for they are one's adversaries.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Better one's own dharma, though imperfect, than the dharma of another well performed; better is death in one's own dharma — the dharma of another is fraught with fear.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Arjuna asks what impels a person to sin even against his will; Kṛṣṇa answers: it is desire, it is anger, born of rajas, all-devouring and very sinful — know it as the enemy here; as fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust and an embryo by the womb, so knowledge is covered by it — the constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, an insatiable fire.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The senses, the mind and the understanding are said to be its seat; through them it deludes the embodied one, veiling knowledge; therefore, first restraining the senses, slay this sinful destroyer of knowledge and realization.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The senses, they say, are high; higher than the senses is the mind, higher than the mind is the understanding, and higher than the understanding is he; knowing him who is beyond the understanding, steadying the self by the self, slay the enemy in the form of desire, so hard to overcome.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: Parallel: Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.3.10.

paraphrase: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvat; Vivasvat told it to Manu and Manu to Ikṣvāku; handed down thus in succession the royal sages knew it; by long lapse of time the yoga was lost here; that same ancient yoga I have told you today, because you are my devotee and friend — it is the highest secret.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Arjuna asks how Kṛṣṇa, born later, could have taught Vivasvat; Kṛṣṇa answers that many births of his and of Arjuna's have passed — he knows them all, Arjuna does not.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Though I am unborn, of imperishable self, and the Lord of beings, yet governing my own prakṛti I come into being by my own māyā.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and a rise of adharma, I send myself forth; for the protection of the good, the destruction of evil-doers and the establishment of dharma I come into being age after age.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Children, not the wise, speak of Sāṃkhya and Yoga as different; one who is established in even one of them obtains the fruit of both; the state reached by the Sāṃkhyas is reached by the yogins too — one who sees Sāṃkhya and Yoga as one, sees.

paraphrase: Renunciation is hard to attain without yoga; the sage yoked in yoga soon reaches Brahman.

paraphrase: The one yoked in yoga, pure, self-conquered, whose self has become the self of all beings, is not tainted though acting; the knower of truth, yoked, thinks 'I do nothing at all' while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, breathing, speaking, letting go, grasping, opening and closing the eyes — holding that the senses move among their objects.

paraphrase: One who acts offering actions to Brahman, abandoning attachment, is not touched by sin, as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water.

paraphrase: Yogins perform action with body, mind, understanding and the senses alone, abandoning attachment, for the purification of the self; the yoked one, abandoning the fruit of action, attains lasting peace, while the unyoked, attached to the fruit through desire, is bound.

paraphrase: Renouncing all actions by the mind, the self-controlled embodied one dwells happily in the city of nine gates, neither acting nor causing action.

paraphrase: The Lord does not create agency or actions for the world, nor the union of action with its fruit; it is inherent nature (svabhāva) that acts; the all-pervading one takes on no one's sin or merit; knowledge is veiled by ignorance, and by that beings are deluded.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: But for those whose ignorance is destroyed by knowledge of the self, that knowledge, like the sun, reveals the supreme; with their understanding in That, their self That, established in That, devoted to That, they go to non-return, their faults shaken off by knowledge.

paraphrase: Knowing me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all the worlds, the friend of all beings, one attains peace.

paraphrase: By the delusion of the pairs of opposites arising from desire and aversion, all beings fall into delusion at birth; but people of meritorious deeds whose sin has come to an end, freed from the delusion of opposites, worship me firm in their vows.

paraphrase: Those who, taking refuge in me, strive for release from old age and death know that Brahman, the whole of what concerns the self (adhyātma) and all action; those who know me together with what concerns beings, the divine and sacrifice, know me even at the time of departure, with yoked minds.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Arjuna asks what Brahman is, what adhyātma, what action, what adhibhūta and adhidaiva, who the adhiyajña in this body is and how, and how Kṛṣṇa is to be known by the self-controlled at the time of departure.
speaker: Arjuna

paraphrase: The Imperishable is the supreme Brahman; its own nature is called adhyātma; the creative offering that brings beings into existence is called action; adhibhūta is perishable existence; the Puruṣa is the adhidaivata; and I myself am the adhiyajña here in the body.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Whoever at the time of death leaves the body remembering me alone goes to my state; of this there is no doubt.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Therefore at all times remember me and fight; with mind and understanding fixed on me you will come to me without doubt.

paraphrase: One who meditates with a mind yoked by the yoga of practice and not straying elsewhere goes to the supreme divine Puruṣa; one who at the time of departure, with unmoving mind, yoked with devotion and the power of yoga, sets the breath fully between the eyebrows and meditates on the seer, the ancient, the ruler, subtler than the subtle, the supporter of all, of unthinkable form, sun-coloured beyond darkness, reaches that supreme divine Puruṣa.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: That which the knowers of the Veda call the Imperishable, which ascetics free from passion enter, desiring which they practise celibacy — that state I will declare to you briefly.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: Parallel: Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.2.15.

paraphrase: Closing all the gates of the body, confining the mind in the heart, placing his breath in the head, established in yogic concentration, uttering Oṃ, the one-syllabled Brahman, and remembering me, one who departs, leaving the body, goes to the supreme goal.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Uttering Oṃ, the one-syllabled Brahman, and remembering me, whoever departs leaving the body goes to the supreme goal.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: For the yogin who is ever yoked and remembers me constantly with undivided mind, I am easily attained.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Having come to me, the great souls do not again take birth, which is the transient abode of sorrow, for they have reached the highest perfection; all worlds up to the world of Brahmā are subject to return, but for one who reaches me there is no rebirth.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Those who know that the day of Brahmā lasts a thousand ages and his night a thousand ages know day and night; at the coming of day all manifest things arise from the unmanifest, and at the coming of night they dissolve into that same unmanifest; this same multitude of beings, arising again and again, dissolves helplessly at the coming of night and arises at the coming of day.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Beyond this unmanifest there is another eternal unmanifest being which does not perish when all beings perish; it is called the Imperishable and is the supreme goal, reaching which they do not return — that is my supreme abode; that supreme Puruṣa, in whom beings abide and by whom all this is pervaded, is to be won by undivided devotion.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: I will tell the times at which yogins depart to return or not to return: fire, light, day, the bright fortnight, the six months of the sun's northern course — departing then the knowers of Brahman go to Brahman; smoke, night, the dark fortnight, the six months of the southern course — departing then the yogin reaches the lunar light and returns; these two paths of the world, the bright and the dark, are held to be eternal: by one a person goes to non-return, by the other he returns again.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: Parallel: Chāndogya Upaniṣad 5.10 and Bṛhadāraṇyaka 6.2.15–16 (the paths of the gods and of the ancestors). Commentators read fire, day, etc. as presiding deities of stages on the path.

paraphrase: Knowing these two paths, no yogin is deluded; therefore be yoked in yoga at all times; knowing this, the yogin goes beyond the merit declared for the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities and gifts, and reaches the supreme primal abode.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: To you who do not cavil I will declare this most secret knowledge together with realization, knowing which you will be freed from ill; it is the royal knowledge, the royal secret, the supreme purifier, known by direct perception, in accord with dharma, very easy to practise and imperishable.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: People who have no faith in this dharma, not reaching me, return to the path of death and saṃsāra.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: By me in my unmanifest form all this world is pervaded; all beings abide in me, but I do not abide in them; and yet beings do not abide in me — behold my divine yoga: my self sustains beings and brings them into being, yet does not abide in them.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: Śaṅkara reads the non-abiding of beings in the Lord as pointing to the unreality of the world from the ultimate standpoint; the Vaiṣṇava commentators as the Lord's independence of what he supports.

paraphrase: As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, always abides in space, so all beings abide in me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: At the end of a kalpa all beings pass into my prakṛti, and at the beginning of a kalpa I send them forth again; resting on my own prakṛti I send forth again and again this whole multitude of beings, helpless under the power of prakṛti; these actions do not bind me, seated as one indifferent and unattached to them; with me as overseer, prakṛti brings forth the moving and the unmoving, and by this cause the world revolves.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The deluded disregard me when I have taken a human body, not knowing my higher being as the great Lord of beings; with vain hopes, vain actions and vain knowledge, senseless, they share the deluding nature of rākṣasas and asuras.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: But the great souls, resorting to the divine nature, worship me with undistracted minds, knowing me as the imperishable origin of beings; always singing my praise, striving, firm in their vows, bowing to me with devotion, ever yoked, they worship me; others, sacrificing with the sacrifice of knowledge, worship me as the One, as distinct, and as manifold, facing every way.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: 9.15's 'as one, as distinct, as manifold' is read by commentators as naming different modes of contemplating the Lord.

paraphrase: I am the ritual, the sacrifice, the offering to the ancestors, the healing herb, the mantra, the clarified butter, the fire and the oblation; I am the father of this world, its mother, supporter and grandsire, the object of knowledge, the purifier, the syllable Oṃ, the Ṛk, the Sāman and the Yajus; the goal, supporter, lord, witness, abode, refuge and friend; the origin and dissolution, the ground, the treasure-house and the imperishable seed; I give heat, withhold and send forth the rain; I am immortality and death, being and non-being.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Knowers of the three Vedas, drinkers of soma, purified of sin, worship me with sacrifices and pray for the way to heaven; reaching the holy world of Indra they enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods; having enjoyed the vast world of heaven, their merit exhausted, they enter the world of mortals; thus following the dharma of the three Vedas, desiring desires, they obtain going and returning.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Those people who, thinking of nothing else, worship me, ever devoted — for them I bear the burden of their gain and security.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: I am the same to all beings; none is hateful to me and none dear; but those who worship me with devotion are in me and I am in them.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Even if one of very evil conduct worships me with undivided devotion, he should be considered righteous, for he has resolved rightly; he quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace — know for certain that my devotee does not perish.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Those who take refuge in me, even though they be of sinful birth — women, vaiśyas and śūdras — they too reach the highest goal; how much more then holy brāhmaṇas and devoted royal sages; having come to this transient, joyless world, worship me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Of creations I am the beginning, the end and the middle; among sciences I am the knowledge of the self; of those who argue I am the reasoning; among letters I am the letter A and of compounds the dvandva; I am imperishable Time and the creator facing every way.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Whatever is the seed of all beings, that I am; there is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist without me; there is no end to my divine manifestations — what I have told is only an illustration; whatever being has glory, grace or power, know that it has sprung from a fragment of my splendour; but what need have you of this detailed knowledge? I stand, supporting this whole world with a single fragment of myself.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Arjuna says his delusion has gone through the supreme secret teaching about the self that Kṛṣṇa has spoken, and asks, if Kṛṣṇa thinks it possible for him to see it, to be shown his imperishable sovereign form.
speaker: Arjuna

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa bids him behold his forms by hundreds and thousands, divine, of many colours and shapes, and the whole world, moving and unmoving, gathered in one in his body; but since Arjuna cannot see him with his own eye, he gives him a divine eye to behold his sovereign yoga.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Sañjaya describes the form: many mouths and eyes, many wondrous sights, divine ornaments and raised divine weapons, divine garlands and garments and perfumes, all-wonderful, infinite, facing every way; if the light of a thousand suns were to rise at once in the sky it might resemble the splendour of that great being; there Arjuna saw the whole universe with its many divisions gathered in one in the body of the god of gods; overcome with wonder, his hair standing on end, he bowed his head and spoke with joined palms.
speaker: Sañjaya

paraphrase: Arjuna's vision and praise: in the body of the god he sees the gods, Brahmā seated on the lotus, the seers and serpents; the form without beginning, middle or end, blazing like fire and sun; he sees the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the warriors of both sides rushing into its terrible mouths, some caught between the teeth with crushed heads, as rivers rush to the ocean and moths into a blazing fire; terrified, he asks who he is in this fierce form.
speaker: Arjuna

paraphrase: I am Time, grown mighty, the destroyer of worlds, now engaged in destroying the worlds; even without you, none of the warriors arrayed in the opposing armies will survive.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Arjuna's hymn: rightly the world rejoices in his praise and the rākṣasas flee; he is the first god, the ancient Puruṣa, the supreme resting place of the universe, Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the moon, Prajāpati and the great-grandsire — 'salutations, salutations to you a thousand times'; Arjuna asks forgiveness for having called him familiarly 'O Kṛṣṇa, O Yādava, O friend', not knowing his greatness, and asks him to bear with him as a father with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved; delighted yet afraid, he asks to see again his four-armed form.

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa tells Arjuna not to be afraid or bewildered and shows him again his former, gentle form; seeing the gentle human form Arjuna is composed and restored to his nature.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see; even the gods ever long to see it; not by the Vedas, austerity, gifts or sacrifice can I be seen as you have seen me; but by undivided devotion I can be known in this form, seen in truth, and entered.

paraphrase: By undivided devotion, Arjuna, I can be known and seen in this form in truth, and entered.

paraphrase: One by whom the world is not agitated and who is not agitated by the world, who is free from elation, anger, fear and anxiety; who is without expectation, pure, skilful, impartial, untroubled, renouncing all undertakings; who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor desires, and has given up good and evil — such a devotee is dear to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: One who is the same to foe and friend, in honour and dishonour, in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, free from attachment; the same in blame and praise, silent, content with whatever comes, without a home, steady-minded, full of devotion — that person is dear to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Those who with faith, holding me supreme, follow this nectar of dharma as declared, those devotees are exceedingly dear to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: This body is called the field (kṣetra); one who knows it is called the knower of the field (kṣetrajña) by those who know them; know me also as the knower of the field in all fields; the knowledge of the field and its knower is, in my view, knowledge.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Hear from me briefly what the field is, of what kind, with what modifications and whence, and who the knower is and what his powers; this has been sung by the seers in many ways, in distinct Vedic metres, and in the well-reasoned and decisive words of the Brahma-sūtra.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: Whether 'brahmasūtrapadaiḥ' refers to Bādarāyaṇa's Brahma Sūtra is disputed: Śaṅkara glosses it as Upaniṣadic statements indicating Brahman, Rāmānuja as the Śārīraka sūtras (moderate confidence on these glosses).

paraphrase: The great elements, ego, understanding and the unmanifest, the ten senses and the one (the mind), and the five objects of the senses; desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate (of body and senses), consciousness and steadfastness — this in brief is the field with its modifications.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: The list gives the twenty-four principles of the Sāṃkhya enumeration (five elements, ego, intellect, the unmanifest, eleven organs, five objects) plus seven further items.

paraphrase: What is called knowledge: absence of pride and pretence, non-harm, patience, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadiness, self-restraint; dispassion toward sense-objects, absence of ego, seeing the evil of birth, death, old age, disease and pain; non-attachment, not clinging to son, wife and home, constant evenness of mind in the desired and the undesired; unswerving devotion to me with undivided yoga, resorting to solitary places, distaste for the company of crowds; constancy in the knowledge of the self and insight into the goal of knowledge of the truth — this is declared to be knowledge; what is contrary is ignorance.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: I will declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality: the beginningless supreme Brahman, which is said to be neither being nor non-being.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: With hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and faces everywhere, with ears everywhere, it stands enveloping everything in the world; shining through the functions of all the senses yet free of all senses, unattached yet supporting all, free of the guṇas yet experiencing the guṇas; outside and inside beings, unmoving and moving, too subtle to be known, far and yet near; undivided yet standing as if divided among beings, the supporter of beings, their devourer and creator; the light of lights, said to be beyond darkness, knowledge, the knowable and the goal of knowledge, seated in the heart of all.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: 13.13–14 closely parallel Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 3.16–17.

paraphrase: Thus the field, knowledge and the knowable have been briefly told; my devotee, understanding this, attains my state.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Know that prakṛti and puruṣa are both beginningless, and that the modifications and guṇas are born of prakṛti; prakṛti is called the cause in the producing of effect, instrument and agency, puruṣa the cause in the experiencing of pleasure and pain; puruṣa, seated in prakṛti, experiences the guṇas born of prakṛti, and attachment to the guṇas is the cause of his births in good and evil wombs; the supreme Puruṣa in this body is called the witness, the permitter, the supporter, the experiencer, the great Lord and the supreme self; one who thus knows puruṣa and prakṛti with its guṇas is not born again, however he may live.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: Range summary; 13.19–20, 13.22 and 13.23 recorded individually.

paraphrase: Know that prakṛti and puruṣa are both beginningless, and that the modifications and the guṇas arise from prakṛti; prakṛti is said to be the cause in the production of effect, instrument and agency, and puruṣa the cause in the experiencing of pleasure and pain.

paraphrase: One who thus knows puruṣa and prakṛti together with the guṇas is not born again, however he may be living.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Some by meditation see the self in the self by the self; others by the yoga of Sāṃkhya, and others by the yoga of action; still others, not knowing this, worship having heard it from others — they too, devoted to what they have heard, cross beyond death.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: An anchor for P3 (plural paths) and P4 (even those who only hear and worship cross beyond death).

paraphrase: Whatever being is born, moving or unmoving, know that it arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: One who sees the supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, the imperishable within the perishing, sees; seeing the Lord established equally everywhere, he does not injure the self by the self and so goes to the supreme goal.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: One who sees that all actions are performed by prakṛti alone and that the self is not the doer, sees; when one sees the separate existence of beings as resting in the One and their expansion from that alone, one attains Brahman.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: This imperishable supreme self, being beginningless and without guṇas, though dwelling in the body neither acts nor is tainted; as all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, so the self present everywhere in the body is not tainted; as the one sun illumines this whole world, so the knower of the field illumines the whole field.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Those who with the eye of knowledge know the difference between the field and the knower of the field, and the liberation of beings from prakṛti, go to the supreme.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: I will declare again the supreme knowledge, highest of all knowledge, knowing which all the sages passed from here to supreme perfection; resorting to this knowledge and having attained a nature like mine, they are not born at creation nor disturbed at dissolution.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: 'sādharmya' (likeness of nature) is read by Vaiṣṇava commentators as a liberated state distinct from identity, by Śaṅkara as attaining the Lord's own nature.

paraphrase: The great Brahman (mahad brahma) is my womb; in it I place the seed, and from that is the birth of all beings; whatever forms are born in any womb, great Brahman is their womb and I am the seed-giving father.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Sattva, rajas and tamas — the guṇas born of prakṛti — bind the imperishable embodied one in the body.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Sattva, being stainless, illuminating and free of disease, binds by attachment to happiness and to knowledge; rajas, whose nature is passion, arising from thirst and attachment, binds the embodied one by attachment to action; tamas, born of ignorance and deluding all embodied beings, binds by negligence, sloth and sleep.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Sattva attaches to happiness, rajas to action, while tamas, veiling knowledge, attaches to negligence; sattva prevails by overpowering rajas and tamas, rajas by overpowering sattva and tamas, and tamas by overpowering sattva and rajas.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: When the light of knowledge shines through all the gates of this body, know that sattva has increased; greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and longing arise when rajas increases; darkness, inertia, negligence and delusion arise when tamas increases.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: If the embodied one meets death when sattva prevails, he goes to the pure worlds of those who know the highest; dying in rajas he is born among those attached to action; dying in tamas he is born in the wombs of the deluded.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The fruit of good action is said to be sāttvic and pure, the fruit of rajas sorrow, the fruit of tamas ignorance; from sattva knowledge arises, from rajas greed, from tamas negligence, delusion and ignorance; those established in sattva go upward, the rājasic stay in the middle, and the tāmasic, abiding in the lowest guṇa, go downward.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: When the seer beholds no agent other than the guṇas and knows what is beyond the guṇas, he attains my being; going beyond these three guṇas from which the body arises, the embodied one, freed from birth, death, old age and sorrow, attains immortality.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Arjuna asks: by what marks is one known who has gone beyond these three guṇas, what is his conduct, and how does he pass beyond them?
speaker: Arjuna

paraphrase: He does not hate illumination, activity and delusion when they arise, nor long for them when they cease; seated as one indifferent, he is not disturbed by the guṇas and, knowing that it is the guṇas that act, stands firm and does not waver; the same in pleasure and pain, abiding in the self, regarding a clod, a stone and gold as equal, the same toward the pleasant and the unpleasant, steady, the same in blame and praise; the same in honour and dishonour, to friend and foe, renouncing all undertakings — he is said to have gone beyond the guṇas.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: One who serves me with the unswerving yoga of devotion, passing beyond these guṇas, becomes fit for becoming Brahman.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The divine endowment (daivī sampad): fearlessness, purity of being, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, giving, self-restraint, sacrifice, study of scripture, austerity, uprightness; non-harm, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, peace, absence of slander, compassion for beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness; vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of malice and of excessive pride — these belong to one born to the divine endowment.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Hypocrisy, arrogance, pride, anger, harshness and ignorance belong to one born to the demonic endowment.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The divine endowment is held to lead to liberation, the demonic to bondage; do not grieve, you are born to the divine endowment.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: There are two kinds of beings in this world, the divine and the demonic; the demonic know neither the way of action nor the way of withdrawal (pravṛtti and nivṛtti); neither purity nor good conduct nor truth is found in them.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The Gītā reports the view of the demonic: they say the world is without truth, without foundation, without a Lord, not produced in any order but arising from mutual union, with desire as its cause — what else?
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: A materialist-type view reported, and rejected, by the Gītā itself (reporting source: src:bhagavad-gita); commentators identify it with the Lokāyata.

paraphrase: Holding this view, these lost souls of small understanding and cruel deeds rise up as enemies of the world for its destruction; given to insatiable desire, full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, they act with impure resolves; beset by innumerable cares ending only with death, they think: 'this I have gained today, this desire I shall fulfil; this enemy I have slain and others I shall slay; I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am successful, powerful and happy'; self-conceited, they sacrifice in name only, with ostentation and not according to rule, and hate me in their own bodies and in others'.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: These cruel haters, the worst of men, I hurl again and again into demonic wombs in the cycles of saṃsāra; entering demonic wombs birth after birth, deluded, not attaining me, they go to the lowest state.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Threefold is this gate of hell, destructive of the self: desire, anger and greed; therefore one should abandon these three; a person released from these three gates of darkness practises what is good for himself and then goes to the supreme goal.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Śaṅkara's introduction: the Lord created the world and established the twofold Vedic dharma of activity (pravṛtti) and withdrawal (nivṛtti); when dharma declined, Viṣṇu was born as Kṛṣṇa, and the Gītā teaches both, its purpose being the highest good through steadfastness in the knowledge of the self preceded by renunciation of all works.
Nārāyaṇa, the supreme Brahman, to be reached only by devotion arising from one's own dharma, knowledge and detachment, is proclaimed in the Gītā-śāstra.

In the first six chapters the yogas of knowledge and action, accompanied by self-knowledge, are taught as the means to the vision of the self; in the middle six, bhakti-yoga, brought about by knowledge and action, for the attainment of the Lord; in the last six, what was taught earlier (prakṛti, puruṣa, the Lord, the yogas) is clarified.

Madhusūdana's introduction: the Gītā has three sections of six chapters each — on action, on devotion (upāsanā) and on knowledge — corresponding to the three parts of the Veda; the first teaches the meaning of 'thou', the second of 'that', the third their identity.

Tilak argues that the Gītā's principal teaching is karma-yoga: the one who has realized Brahman should go on acting for the welfare of the world (lokasaṃgraha) without attachment, rather than renounce action; knowledge and devotion support such action.
